claims.text: To make image-model infographics part of the newsroom's workflow, the team ran a bake-off on 10 October to answer which model, for which job, at what cost.
claims.quote: So on 10 October we ran a bake-off, and this is what it found.

claims.text: The field was every image-output model OpenRouter offered that day, five from Google, three from OpenAI, its auto-router, and the newsroom's code-drawn renderer as a $0 control.
claims.quote: five from Google, three from OpenAI, its auto-router, and our code-drawn renderer as a $0 control

claims.text: Eleven briefs, all from one article, from an 18-word stat card to the whole 2,800-word article, plus an edit, a UI component, a brand slide and a three-slide deck.
claims.quote: Eleven, all from one article

claims.text: Every image was judged blind by a Designer agent under a random id, with a fact check of every required string, anything invented, six criteria and an overall score.
claims.quote: Every image judged blind by a Designer agent

claims.text: The bill was 101 images for $10.44, half of it paid for images the judge would not use.
claims.quote: The bill. 101 images, $10.44. Half of it paid for images the judge would not use.

claims.text: The Accountant's rule is that a failed image was still paid for, so the number that matters is cost per usable image, not price per image.
claims.quote: the number that matters is cost per usable image, not price per image

claims.text: The Data Scientist makes the cut after each round and must not promote or drop a model on a difference smaller than the noise.
claims.quote: must not promote or drop a model on a difference smaller than the noise

claims.text: Spelling turned out to be mostly solved; only Gemini 2.5 Flash Image misspelled labels, and the faults were obedience and format.
claims.quote: Spelling turned out to be mostly solved: only one model, Gemini 2.5 Flash Image, misspelled labels.

claims.text: GPT-5 Image and GPT-5 Image Mini ignore the requested aspect ratio and always return a 1024 square.
claims.quote: GPT-5 Image and GPT-5 Image Mini ignore the requested aspect ratio and always return a 1024 square.

claims.text: On the chart with fourteen exact values, five of six models drew every bar right, sorted and in proportion.
claims.quote: Five of six models drew every bar right, sorted and in proportion

value.unit: models with every chart value right

claims.text: On the document and whole-article briefs GPT-5.4 Image 2 scored 9 on both, the only model with every number right and the whole argument told.
claims.quote: GPT-5.4 Image 2 scored 9 on both

value.unit: blind score out of 10 on the document briefs

claims.text: Give the newest model the document, not a description of the picture; the older GPT-5 Image got worse with more text, and the Google models dropped caveats and invented sample values.
claims.quote: Give it the document, not a description of the picture.

claims.text: Running the diagram brief twice unchanged measured the noise: scores moved by up to two points between identical runs, so one image per cell separates tiers, not neighbours.
claims.quote: scores moved by up to two points between identical runs

value.unit: points of score between identical runs

claims.text: On the edit, only GPT-5.4 Image 2 made all three changes without breaking anything; every Google model treated the edit as a redraw and something else moved.
claims.quote: Only GPT-5.4 Image 2 made all three changes without breaking anything (9).

claims.text: Nano Banana 2.1, the best value of the first two rounds, had no usable image in round 3: the briefs where every character is specified are the ones it loosens.
claims.quote: the briefs where every character is specified are the ones it loosens

claims.text: In the deck round no model carried the cover's top bar or footer to the other slides, because nothing in a separate call knows what the last slide looked like.
claims.quote: nothing in a separate call knows what the last slide looked like

claims.text: Sending slide 1 with every later slide fixed consistency: judged blind in pairs, every model's referenced set was the more consistent one, from 1 or 2 out of 5 to 4 or 5.
claims.quote: every model's referenced set was the more consistent one

claims.text: Nano Banana 2.1 is the pick for concept slides, charts and decks at about $0.04 an image.
claims.quote: Nano Banana 2.1 for concept slides, charts and decks (about $0.04 an image)

claims.text: GPT-5.4 Image 2 is the pick for documents, whole articles, edits, components and brand slides, at about $0.17 to $0.23 and 60 to 120 seconds.
claims.quote: GPT-5.4 Image 2 for documents, whole articles, edits, components and brand slides (about $0.17 to $0.23, 60 to 120 seconds)

claims.text: Half the money, $4.43 of the first $8.80, bought images nobody would use; price per image flatters a model that fails often, cost per usable image does not.
claims.quote: Half the money bought images nobody would use ($4.43 of the first $8.80).

claims.text: Gemini 3 Pro Image is not cheaper than GPT-5.4 Image 2 per usable image, but it is four times faster, and the guidance uses it only where waiting matters.
claims.quote: It is four times faster. That is its case

claims.text: A newsroom month of twelve images a day on the recommended mix costs about $40, a cost per article of about $1.34 the owner is happy to pay and to show.
claims.quote: A cost per article of about $1.34 is one I am happy to pay, and to show.

value.unit: USD per article on the recommended mix

claims.text: The prompt rules the faults taught: never name the platform, because suitable for LinkedIn put LinkedIn logos on the image; end with no other text; say no numbers other than those given.
claims.quote: "Suitable for LinkedIn" put LinkedIn logos on the image.

claims.text: OCR and the judge agreed on 76% of images: OCR is a cheap alarm, not a judge, so every image must be checked.
claims.quote: OCR and the judge agreed on 76% of images: OCR is a cheap alarm, not a judge.

value.unit: percent of images where OCR and the judge agreed

claims.text: The samples are small: most cells hold one or two images and identical runs moved by up to two points, so the tiers hold but a one-point gap means little.
claims.quote: Most cells hold one or two images, and identical runs moved by up to two points.

claims.text: There is one judge and one rubric, an agent judging blind; a person would weigh craft differently, though the fact checks would not change.
claims.quote: A person would weigh craft differently; the fact checks would not change.

claims.text: Prices, models and behaviour are OpenRouter's on 10 October 2026, one day; the runner, scorer and briefs are in the vault so it can be run again.
claims.quote: Prices, models and their behaviour are OpenRouter's on 10 October 2026.

claims.text: Only what OpenRouter offers was tested; other image models exist outside it, and this is the set one key could reach.
claims.quote: Other image models exist outside it; this is the set one key could reach.

claims.text: The guidance becomes the Storyteller's, and the bake-off runs again whenever a new model appears, because the answer to which model has a date on it.
claims.quote: the bake-off runs again whenever a new model appears, because the answer to "which model" has a date on it

claims.text: The article was written by agent@riskmandate.ai on Claude Opus 5.5 from a voice memo, and is disclosed as AI-generated as Article 50 of the EU AI Act asks.
claims.quote: AI-generated, disclosed as Article 50 of the EU AI Act asks.

claims.text: Everything is in a vault as an app: the briefs, all 101 images, every score and reason, the ledger, the analysis and the guidance.
claims.quote: the briefs, all 101 images, every score and reason, the ledger, the analysis and the guidance, as an app

claims.text: The Designer role is adapted from the SG/Send team's Designer, whose first principle is that an infographic that is beautiful and wrong has failed.
claims.quote: an infographic that is beautiful and wrong has failed
